memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "The west end was fifty cubits wide and had curtains, with ten posts and ten bases, with silver hooks and bands on the posts. The east end, towards the sunrise, was also fifty cubits wide." - Exod 38:12-13 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Look at what holds this boundary up: bronze bases sunk into the ground, and silver hooks holding the curtains at the top.

Two different metals doing two different jobs. Bronze below, where the weight and the dirt were. Silver above, where the curtains hung.

The silver in the tabernacle came from the redemption money each Israelite paid (Exod 30:11-16; 38:25-27). Every hook holding those curtains was made from ransom money — a permanent reminder that this people had been bought.

That is not a detail to rush past. The very things holding up the boundary of God's dwelling were made of redemption.

The same is true of Christian living. Whatever separates us from the world around us is not our own achievement. It is the result of having been ransomed. You are not your own; you were bought at a price (1 Cor 6:19-20).

This changes how we hold our convictions. If our distinctiveness came from our own discipline, we would be insufferable about it. If it came from being purchased, we hold it humbly and gratefully.

Notice too the east end facing the sunrise. The entrance faced the rising sun — the direction of new light each morning.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Do you view your Christian distinctiveness as an achievement or a gift?
2. What does it mean to you that you were bought at a price?
3. Where has pride crept into how you hold your convictions?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord, everything that sets me apart came from Your ransom, not my effort. Keep me humble and grateful. Amen.
